 By Mark Zeigler | mark.zeigler@sduniontribune.com PUBLISHED: November 15, 2026 at 7:00 AM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... San Diego State vs. New Mexico State
 When: 1 p.m. Sunday
 Where: Frontwave Arena, Oceanside
 On the air: The CW; 760-AM
 Records: SDSU is 3-0; New Mexico State is 1-2.
 Series history: SDSU leads 5-3. The most recent meeting was in the opening round of the 2014 NCAA Tournament in Spokane, Wash., a 73-69 Aztecs win in overtime.
 Aggies update: They beat Division II Western New Mexico in the opener, then got blown out by Gonzaga 109-68 and lost a nail-biter against rival UTEP 60-58 on Thursday after going scoreless for the final 2:58. Jermaine Washington missed a 3-pointer at the buzzer for the win. Mark Lavrenov, a 6-foot-8 transfer from Sacramento State, is the leading scorer (16.7 points per game) and rebounder (7.3 rebounds per game). DJ Dudley, a transfer guard from Louisiana Tech and a preseason all-conference pick, averages 12.0 points. Washington, who grew up in Hemet, is the only other player in double figures at 10.0. Jason Hooten is in his fourth year as head coach. They’ve struggled even more than SDSU to take care of the ball, averaging turnovers on 28.5% of possessions, which currently ranks 359th out of 365 Division I programs. (The Aztecs are 312th at 22.5%). The Aggies were picked to finish sixth in the Conference USA coaches poll after going 16-16 overall and finishing eighth at 8-12 last season. However, they’re currently second-best in the league at 140 in the Kenpom metric, which projects a 78-68 SDSU victory.
 Aztecs update: This is their third of at least a dozen road games this season and the second in as many weekends in a San Diego County venue other than Viejas Arena. Last Saturday, they beat Colorado 77-66 at Pechanga Arena in the Bill Walton Classic. The Frontwave game is called Compete 4 Cause Classic. Because of an arena conflict, the Aztecs weren’t able to practice at Frontwave on Saturday and went there last week instead to familiarize themselves with the sightlines. Several current Aztecs were teammates with New Mexico State players: Jeremiah “Bear” Cherry with Lavrenov at Sacramento State last season, Latrell Davis with Washington and 7-0 Adrame Diongue at San Jose State in 2024-25, and Tae Simmons with DeLan Grant at Heritage Christian High School in Northridge. The focus, once again, is limiting turnovers after coughing up 15, 20 and 15 in the opening three games —16 total more than their opponents. Freshman Zach White has yet to play in the regular season but returned to practice and is expected to be available.
 Next up: Wednesday vs. Texas Southern at Viejas Arena (7 p.m., Pac-12 YouTube Channel)
 — MARK ZEIGLER
